Tafsir of Surah Tabbat

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Salam narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to al-Batha', climbed the mountain, and called out, "Yā ṣabāḥāh!" Quraysh gathered around him, and he said, "Tell me, if I were to inform you that an enemy was going to attack you in the morning or in the evening, would you believe me?" They said, "Yes." He said, "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said, "Is this why you gathered us? Ruin to you!" So Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ to its end [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4972).]].

In another narration: he stood up shaking his hands, saying, "Ruin to you for the whole day! Is this why you gathered us?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (1394, 4801, 3525).]].

The first is an invocation against him, and the second is a report about him. This Abu Lahab was one of the paternal uncles of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). His name was 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, and his kunya was Abu 'Utba. He was called "Abu Lahab" (Father of the Flame) because of the brightness of his face. He was greatly harmful to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), hostile toward him, contemptuous of him, and disparaging of him and his religion.

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-'Abbas narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from his father, who said: A man told me, called Rabi'a ibn 'Abbad, of the Banu al-Dil, who had been a pre-Islamic man and then embraced Islam, said: "I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Jahiliyya, in the market of Dhu al-Majaz, saying, 'O people, say: there is no god but Allah, and you will prosper,' while people gathered around him. Behind him was a man with a bright face, squinting, with two locks of hair, saying, 'He is a lying apostate.' He followed him wherever he went. I asked about him, and they said, 'This is his uncle, Abu Lahab.'"

[[Al-Musnad (4/341).]]

Then he narrated it from Surayj, from Ibn Abi al-Zinad, from his father, and mentioned it. Abu al-Zinad said: I said to Rabi'a, "Were you young at that time?" He said, "No, by Allah, I was then old enough to understand that I was carrying a waterskin." Ahmad alone narrated it [[Al-Musnad (4/341).]].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abbas narrated to me, saying: I heard Rabi'a ibn 'Abbad al-Dili say: "I was with my father, a young man, looking at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) following the tribes, with a man behind him who was squinting, bright-faced, with thick hair. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would stop at a tribe and say, 'O Banu so-and-so, I am the Messenger of Allah to you. I command you to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him, and to believe me and protect me until I convey from Allah what He has sent me with.' When he finished his speech, the other man behind him would say, 'O Banu so-and-so, this man wants you to abandon al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and your allies among the jinn from the Banu Malik ibn Uqaysh, for what he has brought of innovation and misguidance. So do not listen to him or follow him.'" I asked my father, "Who is this?" He said, "His uncle, Abu Lahab" [[See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham (1/423).]].

Ahmad also narrated it, and al-Tabarani with this wording [[Al-Musnad (3/492) and al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (5/63).]].

As for His saying, ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾, meaning: he has lost and been ruined, and his deeds and efforts have gone astray. ﴿And perish he﴾, meaning: and indeed his ruin and destruction have certainly been realized.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿What his wealth and what he earned will not avail him﴾, Ibn 'Abbas and others said: ﴿and what he earned﴾ means his children. The same was narrated from 'A'isha, Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Hasan, and Ibn Sirin.

It is also mentioned from Ibn Mas'ud that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called his people to faith, Abu Lahab said: "If what my nephew says is true, I will ransom myself on the Day of Resurrection from the punishment with my wealth and my children." So Allah revealed: ﴿What his wealth and what he earned will not avail him﴾.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame﴾, meaning: a fire with sparks, flaming and of intense burning.

﴿And his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾. His wife was among the noblewomen of Quraysh; she was Umm Jamil, whose name was Arwa bint Harb ibn Umayya, and she was the sister of Abu Sufyan. She was a helper to her husband in his disbelief, denial, and obstinacy; therefore on the Day of Resurrection she will be a helper against him in his punishment in the Fire of Hell. For this reason He said: ﴿The carrier of firewood, around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾, meaning: she carries firewood and throws it upon her husband, so that his torment increases, and she is prepared and ready for that.

﴿Around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾. Mujahid and 'Urwa said: "of the palm fiber of the Fire."

It is narrated from Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Thawri, and al-Suddi: ﴿The carrier of firewood﴾ was one who walked about carrying tale-bearing [and Ibn Jarir chose this] [[Addition from M.]].

al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, 'Atiyya al-Jadali, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd: she used to place thorns in the path of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Ibn Jarir chose this.

Ibn Jarir said: It was also said: she used to reproach the Prophet (ﷺ) for poverty, and she used to gather firewood, so she was reproached for that.

Thus he related it, without attributing it to anyone. The correct view is the first, and Allah knows best.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: she had a precious necklace and said, "I will spend it on enmity toward Muhammad." Meaning: Allah repaid her with a rope around her neck of the palm fiber of the Fire.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sulaym [[In A: "Sulayman".]], the client of al-Sha'bi, from al-Sha'bi who said: al-Masad is al-layf (palm fiber).

'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr said: al-Masad is a chain whose length is seventy cubits.

From al-Thawri: it is a necklace of fire, its length seventy cubits.

al-Jawhari said: al-Masad is al-layf (palm fiber). Al-Masad is also a rope of palm fiber or of palm leaves, and it may be of camel hide or camel hair. "I masadtu al-habl amsiduhu masdan" means I twisted the rope well [[Al-Sihah of al-Jawhari, entry "msd" (1/535).]].

Mujahid said: ﴿Around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾ means a collar of iron. Do you not see that the Arabs call the pulley a masad?

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father and Abu Zur'a narrated to us, both saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Ibn Tadrus, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr who said: When ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ was revealed, al-'Awra' Umm Jamil bint Harb came, wailing, with a stone in her hand, saying:

"We have condemned him, we have rejected his religion, we have disobeyed his command."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the mosque with Abu Bakr. When Abu Bakr saw her, he said, "O Messenger of Allah, she is coming, and I fear she will see you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "She will not see me." He recited a Qur'an by which he sought protection, as Allah says: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾ [al-Isra': 45]. She came until she stood before Abu Bakr and did not see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said, "O Abu Bakr, I have been told that your companion has satirized me?" He said, "No, by the Lord of this House, he has not satirized you." She turned away saying, "Quraysh knows that I am the daughter of its chief." He said: al-Walid said in his narration, or in another: Umm Jamil stumbled in her cloak while circumambulating the House, and said, "Wretched is Mudhammam (the reviled one)." Umm Hakim bint 'Abd al-Muttalib said: "I am a strong woman, so I do not speak; I am a skilled woman, so I do not get entangled; we are all from the paternal kin, and Quraysh knows best" [[Musnad al-Humaydi (1/153), and Abu Ya'la in his Musnad (1/53) from the route of Sufyan with this, and its takhrij was mentioned at the commentary of verse 45 of Surat al-Isra'.]].

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id and Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, both saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: When ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ was revealed, the wife of Abu Lahab came while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting with Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr said to him, "If only you would move aside, she would not harm you with anything." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Indeed, she will be prevented from seeing me." She came until she stood before Abu Bakr and said, "O Abu Bakr, your companion has satirized us." Abu Bakr said, "No, by the Lord of this structure, he does not utter poetry nor speak it." She said, "You are indeed a believer," and when she left, Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Did she not see you?" He said: "No, an angel kept shielding me until she left."

Then al-Bazzar said: We do not know it to be narrated with a better chain than this one, from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2294) "Kashf al-Astar"; Abu Ya'la in his Musnad (1/33) from the route of 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb with this. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/144): "In it is 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, who became confused."]].

Some of the scholars said regarding His saying, ﴿Around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾, meaning: around her neck is a rope in the Fire [of Hell], by which she is raised to its edge and then thrown down to its bottom, and so on, perpetually.

Abu al-Khattab ibn Dihya said in his book al-Tanwir [[al-Tanwir fi mawlid al-siraj al-munir by Ibn Dihya al-Kalbi, composed for the king of Irbil. See: Wafayat al-A'yan (3/122).]] (and he narrated this) that "masad" was used for the rope of a bucket, as Abu Hanifa al-Dinawari said in his book al-Nabat: "Every masad is a rope," and he recited in that regard:

"A pulley and an axle, a bar... and a masad of hemp, dragged..."

He said: al-abaq is hemp.

Another said:

"O masad of palm leaves, beware of me... if you are soft and gentle, then I..."

"Whatever you wish of a grey-haired, stubborn old man..."

The scholars said: In this surah there is a clear miracle and an evident proof of prophethood, for since the revelation of His saying, ﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾, He informed of their wretchedness and lack of faith, and it was not decreed for either of them to believe, neither outwardly nor inwardly, neither secretly nor openly. So this is among the strongest decisive proofs of the manifest prophethood.

[End of the tafsir of "Tabbat"; and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.] [[Addition from M, A.]]

Thus he related it, without attributing it to anyone. The correct view is the first, and Allah knows best.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: she had a precious necklace and said, "I will spend it on enmity toward Muhammad." Meaning: Allah repaid her with a rope around her neck of the palm fiber of the Fire.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sulaym [[In A: "Sulayman".]], the client of al-Sha'bi, from al-Sha'bi who said: al-Masad is al-layf (palm fiber).

'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr said: al-Masad is a chain whose length is seventy cubits.

From al-Thawri: it is a necklace of fire, its length seventy cubits.

al-Jawhari said: al-Masad is al-layf (palm fiber). Al-Masad is also a rope of palm fiber or of palm leaves, and it may be of camel hide or camel hair. "I masadtu al-habl amsiduhu masdan" means I twisted the rope well [[Al-Sihah of al-Jawhari, entry "msd" (1/535).]].

Mujahid said: ﴿Around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾ means a collar of iron. Do you not see that the Arabs call the pulley a masad?

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father and Abu Zur'a narrated to us, both saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Ibn Tadrus, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr who said: When ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ was revealed, al-'Awra' Umm Jamil bint Harb came, wailing, with a stone in her hand, saying:

"We have condemned him, we have rejected his religion, we have disobeyed his command."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the mosque with Abu Bakr. When Abu Bakr saw her, he said, "O Messenger of Allah, she is coming, and I fear she will see you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "She will not see me." He recited a Qur'an by which he sought protection, as Allah says: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾ [al-Isra': 45]. She came until she stood before Abu Bakr and did not see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said, "O Abu Bakr, I have been told that your companion has satirized me?" He said, "No, by the Lord of this House, he has not satirized you." She turned away saying, "Quraysh knows that I am the daughter of its chief." He said: al-Walid said in his narration, or in another: Umm Jamil stumbled in her cloak while circumambulating the House, and said, "Wretched is Mudhammam (the reviled one)." Umm Hakim bint 'Abd al-Muttalib said: "I am a strong woman, so I do not speak; I am a skilled woman, so I do not get entangled; we are all from the paternal kin, and Quraysh knows best" [[Musnad al-Humaydi (1/153), and Abu Ya'la in his Musnad (1/53) from the route of Sufyan with this, and its takhrij was mentioned at the commentary of verse 45 of Surat al-Isra'.]].

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id and Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, both saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: When ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾ was revealed, the wife of Abu Lahab came while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting with Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr said to him, "If only you would move aside, she would not harm you with anything." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Indeed, she will be prevented from seeing me." She came until she stood before Abu Bakr and said, "O Abu Bakr, your companion has satirized us." Abu Bakr said, "No, by the Lord of this structure, he does not utter poetry nor speak it." She said, "You are indeed a believer," and when she left, Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Did she not see you?" He said: "No, an angel kept shielding me until she left."

Then al-Bazzar said: We do not know it to be narrated with a better chain than this one, from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2294) "Kashf al-Astar"; Abu Ya'la in his Musnad (1/33) from the route of 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb with this. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/144): "In it is 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, who became confused."]].

Some of the scholars said regarding His saying, ﴿Around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾, meaning: around her neck is a rope in the Fire [of Hell], by which she is raised to its edge and then thrown down to its bottom, and so on, perpetually.

Abu al-Khattab ibn Dihya said in his book al-Tanwir [[al-Tanwir fi mawlid al-siraj al-munir by Ibn Dihya al-Kalbi, composed for the king of Irbil. See: Wafayat al-A'yan (3/122).]] (and he narrated this) that "masad" was used for the rope of a bucket, as Abu Hanifa al-Dinawari said in his book al-Nabat: "Every masad is a rope," and he recited in that regard:

"A pulley and an axle, a bar... and a masad of hemp, dragged..."

He said: al-abaq is hemp.

Another said:

"O masad of palm leaves, beware of me... if you are soft and gentle, then I..."

"Whatever you wish of a grey-haired, stubborn old man..."

The scholars said: In this surah there is a clear miracle and an evident proof of prophethood, for since the revelation of His saying, ﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, around her neck a rope of palm fiber﴾, He informed of their wretchedness and lack of faith, and it was not decreed for either of them to believe, neither outwardly nor inwardly, neither secretly nor openly. So this is among the strongest decisive proofs of the manifest prophethood.

[End of the tafsir of "Tabbat"; and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.] [[Addition from M, A.]]
